land.text: Toshala, the early Bhauma-Kara country of coastal Odisha

predecessors.note: The page names no predecessor in the text opened; the Shailodbhavas ruled Kongoda in the region before (not on the pages opened).

successors.note: "The Bhauma-Kara territory ultimately came under the control of the Somavamshis"; the page dates the takeover only to "the 10th century" (Bhanjas and Somavamshis).

capitals.name: Guhadevapataka (Gohiratikar)
capitals.note: "Their capital was located at Guhadevapataka (or Guheshvarapataka), identified with modern Gohiratikar"; coordinates approximate (researcher's).

rulers.name: Kshemankara-deva (founder)
rulers.note: infobox; the era "begins from year 736 CE" (Panigrahi), Sircar dated it 831

correction.text: Toshala, the early Bhauma-Kara country of coastal Odisha

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Bhauma-Kara row; its Kalinga row ends in 171 CE). Infobox "Established: c. 8th century CE"; the era "begins from year 736 CE" (Panigrahi) while Sircar dated it 831 CE. The page gives no area; the 100 km radius round Bhubaneswar is the researcher's reading of Toshala.

New keyframe. "The dynasty probably ruled most of the coastal Odisha by the time of king Shivakara I (c. 756 or 786)." The Rashtrakuta and Pala invasions of 790-829 "weakened and disintegrated the Bhauma kingdom"; Tribhuvana-Mahadevi I "reunified the kingdom, but the family probably never regained its former power". The page gives no area.

region.text: Toshala, the early Bhauma-Kara country of coastal Odisha

ledger.note: 736: Kshemankara-deva founds the Bhauma-Kara line in Toshala. Infobox "736 - 756: Kshemankara-deva (founder)"; the era "begins from year 736 CE" (Panigrahi; Sircar says 831).

minus.text: Toshala, the early Bhauma-Kara country of coastal Odisha

ledger.note: c. 756 (bridge): the line holds most of coastal Odisha. "The dynasty probably ruled most of the coastal Odisha by the time of king Shivakara I (c. 756 or 786)"; the page dates no conquest.

790: Rashtrakuta invasions begin. "a series of Rashtrakuta and Pala invasions weakened and disintegrated the Bhauma kingdom" (the page places them between 790 and 829); the page names no battle or place.
790: Pala invasions begin (same sentence as the Rashtrakuta invasions, 790-829).
829: the Rashtrakuta and Pala invasions end (the page's span 790-829).

10th century (bridge 950): the Somavamshis take the Bhauma-Kara country. "The Bhauma-Kara territory ultimately came under the control of the Somavamshis"; "The Bhauma-Kara family appears to have suffered from internal strifes starting around c. 880"; the last ruler named is Dandi (c. 916 or 923), followed by Vakula-Mahadevi.
c. 950 (bridge): the Bhauma-Kara line ends. Infobox "Disestablished: c. 10th century CE"; no firmer date on the page.

wars.name: Rashtrakuta and Pala invasions of Odisha
wars.outcome: "a series of Rashtrakuta and Pala invasions weakened and disintegrated the Bhauma kingdom"; Tribhuvana-Mahadevi I later reunified it.
wars.note: No battle, place or leader named on the page.

certainty.note: No frontier is given; coastal Odisha is the only land the page names.

sources.title: Bhauma-Kara dynasty
sources.note: Infobox c. 8th-10th century; era 736 / 831; Guhadevapataka; coastal Odisha; 790-829 invasions; Somavamshi takeover.

notes: Cliopatria has no Bhauma-Kara row. One page only (the Somavamshi page is cited by the somavamshi-dynasty dossier). The page gives no regnal years beyond the infobox's 736-756 and 'c. 916 or 923' for Dandi, so 950 is a convention for 'the 10th century'. The Shailodbhava predecessor and the Bhaumas' Kosala/Kalinga claims are not on the page opened. Gazetteer lacks Gohiratikar, Toshala.
